tables.description: Average monthly returns (Panel A, %), post-ranking betas (Panel B), and average size ln(ME) (Panel C) for 100 portfolios formed on size (NYSE decile breakpoints, rows) then pre-ranking beta (10 groups within each decile, columns), equal-weighted, July 1963-December 1990. Includes All row (beta-group portfolios) and All column (size-decile portfolios).
tables.replication_meaning: Proves correct two-pass portfolio construction: CRSP-Compustat intersection universe, NYSE size breakpoints, within-decile beta sorts with NYSE breakpoints on data-qualified stocks, Dimson sum-beta post-ranking estimation against the CRSP VW market, equal-weighted monthly returns held July-June. The All column validates the size effect (1.52 -> 0.89 %/mo); the flat All row validates the paper's central claim that beta variation unrelated to size earns no premium.
tables.paper_quote: Portfolios are formed yearly. The breakpoints for the size (ME, price times shares outstanding) deciles are determined in June of year t (t = 1963-1990) using all NYSE stocks on CRSP. All NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ stocks that meet the CRSP-COMPUSTAT data requirements are allocated to the 10 size portfolios using the NYSE breakpoints. Each size decile is subdivided into 10 beta portfolios using pre-ranking betas of individual stocks, estimated with 2 to 5 years of monthly returns (as available) ending in June of year t. We use only NYSE stocks that meet the CRSP-COMPUSTAT data requirements to establish the beta breakpoints.
tables.notes: Panel A (returns) and Panel C (ln(ME)) parse complete from OCR (11x11); targets cover All row, All column, Small-ME/Large-ME/ME-5 rows. Panel B (betas) OCR dropped one interior column (10 of 11 values per row); targets restricted to the All column (all 10 size deciles, confirmed by paper prose 'post-ranking betas range from 1.44 ... to 0.92') plus prose-anchored corners (small decile 1.05-1.79; overall min 0.53). Interior Panel B cells excluded as OCR-unverifiable.

tables.description: Properties of 12 portfolios formed on size alone (Panel A) or pre-ranking beta alone (Panel B): average return, post-ranking beta, ln(ME), ln(BE/ME), ln(A/ME), ln(A/BE), E/P dummy, E(+)/P, Firms. Portfolios 2-9 are deciles; 1A/1B and 10A/10B split the extreme deciles. NYSE breakpoints, equal-weighted, July 1963-December 1990.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves correct one-dimensional sort mechanics (deciles with split extremes), the characteristic-averaging convention (time-series avg of monthly portfolio averages), the BE/A/E definitions on Compustat fiscal data with December t-1 ME, and the beta-assignment scheme (stocks carry their size-beta portfolio's post-ranking beta). The flat beta-sorted returns (1A=1.20 vs 10B=1.18 with beta 0.81 vs 1.73) is a headline result.
tables.paper_quote: At the end of June of each year t, 12 portfolios are formed on the basis of ranked values of size (ME) or pre-ranking beta. The pre-ranking betas use 2 to 5 years (as available) of monthly returns ending in June of t. Portfolios 2-9 cover deciles of the ranking variables. The bottom and top 2 portfolios (1A, 1B, 10A, and 10B) split the bottom and top deciles in half. The breakpoints for the ME portfolios are based on ranked values of ME for all NYSE stocks on CRSP. NYSE breakpoints for pre-ranking betas are also used to form the beta portfolios.
tables.notes: OCR correction: Panel A row labels were shifted by one (the 'Return' label was dropped); corrected mapping verified by paper prose (returns 1.64->0.90; betas 1.44->0.90) and the identity ln(A/ME)-ln(A/BE)=ln(BE/ME). Panel A E(+)/P row is missing from the OCR -> excluded. Panel B Return row lost one interior cell -> only prose-anchored 1A and 10B targeted; all other Panel B rows are complete.

tables.description: Time-series averages of slopes (with t-statistics) from month-by-month Fama-MacBeth regressions of individual stock returns on beta, ln(ME), ln(BE/ME), ln(A/ME), ln(A/BE), E/P dummy, and E(+)/P over 11 specifications, July 1963-December 1990. ~2267 stocks per monthly regression; ratios winsorized at 0.005/0.995 fractiles.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the Fama-MacBeth machinery: monthly cross-sectional OLS on individual stocks with portfolio-assigned betas and firm-specific characteristics, correct timing (June t size, December t-1 ratios, July t-June t+1 returns), the 0.5% winsorization of the four ratios, and the E(+)/P / E/P-dummy split. The headline cells — ln(ME) alone -0.15 (-2.58), beta alone 0.15 (0.46), ln(BE/ME) alone 0.50 (5.71) — are the paper's core asset-pricing claims.
tables.paper_quote: The average slope is the time-series average of the monthly regression slopes for July 1963 to December 1990, and the t-statistic is the average slope divided by its time-series standard error. [...] On average, there are 2267 stocks in the monthly regressions. To avoid giving extreme observations heavy weight in the regressions, the smallest and largest 0.5% of the observations on E(+)/P, BE/ME, A/ME, and A/BE are set equal to the next largest or smallest values of the ratios (the 0.005 and 0.995 fractiles).

tables.description: Properties of portfolios formed on BE/ME (Panel A, 12 portfolios 1A-10B) and E/P (Panel B, 13 portfolios with 0 = negative E/P): return, beta, ln(ME), ln(BE/ME), ln(A/ME), ln(A/BE), E/P dummy, E(+)/P, Firms. Breakpoints from ALL data-qualified stocks (not NYSE-only). Formed at end of year t-1, equal-weighted July t-June t+1.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves correct accounting-ratio construction with December t-1 ME (BE/ME and E/P), the negative-E portfolio-0 handling, the all-stock (non-NYSE) breakpoint convention for BE/ME and E/P sorts, and exclusion of negative book equity firms. The BE/ME return spread 0.30 -> 1.83 %/mo (1.53 spread) with flat betas (~1.27-1.36) is the paper's strongest cross-sectional result; the U-shaped E/P pattern (1.46 -> 0.93 -> 1.72) validates the E/P dummy + E(+)/P variable split.
tables.paper_quote: At the end of each year t - 1, 12 portfolios are formed on the basis of ranked values of BE/ME or E/P. [...] For E/P, there are 13 portfolios; portfolio 0 is stocks with negative E/P. Since BE/ME and E/P are not strongly related to exchange listing, their portfolio breakpoints are determined on the basis of the ranked values of the variables for all stocks that satisfy the CRSP-COMPUSTAT data requirements.
tables.notes: OCR correction: Panel A header includes a spurious '0' column (no negative-BE portfolio exists; paper p.441 'we do not include them in the tests'); the 12 data values map to 1A-10B, verified by prose ('returns rise from 0.30% for the lowest BE/ME portfolio to 1.83% for the highest') and monotonic ln(BE/ME). Panel B's first of two 'ln(A/BE)' rows is ln(A/ME), verified via ln(A/ME)-ln(A/BE)=ln(BE/ME).

tables.description: Average monthly returns (%) on 100 portfolios formed on size (NYSE decile breakpoints) then BE/ME (10 groups within each decile, breakpoints within decile), equal-weighted, July 1963-December 1990. BE/ME = (common equity + balance-sheet deferred taxes, fiscal t-1) / ME December t-1.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the two-dimensional size x BE/ME sort with the within-decile BE/ME breakpoints and the December-t-1 ratio timing, and demonstrates the paper's parsimonious model: within each size decile returns rise strongly with BE/ME (avg within-decile spread 0.99%/mo: 1.63-0.64 in the All row), and within each BE/ME group returns decline with size (0.58%/mo: 1.47-0.89 in the All column). This is the empirical foundation of the FF three-factor HML design.
tables.paper_quote: In June of each year t, the NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ stocks that meet the CRSP-COMPUSTAT data requirements are allocated to 10 size portfolios using the NYSE size (ME) breakpoints. The NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ stocks in each size decile are then sorted into 10 BE/ME portfolios using the book-to-market ratios for year t - 1. BE/ME is the book value of common equity plus balance-sheet deferred taxes for fiscal year t - 1, over market equity for December of year t - 1.
tables.notes: Complete 11x11 matrix targeted (all cells). Prose cross-checks: within-decile spread 1.63-0.64 = 0.99%/mo; All-column size spread 1.47-0.89 = 0.58%/mo.

tables.description: Subperiod means, standard deviations and t-statistics for (i) NYSE value- and equal-weighted portfolio returns, (ii) FM regression of returns on ln(ME) + ln(BE/ME), and (iii) FM regression on beta + ln(ME) + ln(BE/ME), over the full period (330 months) and two subperiods (162/168 months).
tables.replication_meaning: Proves temporal robustness and the subperiod stability of the BE/ME effect (slopes 0.36 and 0.35 vs 0.35 full-period; all > 2.95 SE from 0), the insignificance of beta in both subperiods (0.10, t=0.25 in 63-76; -0.44, t=-1.17 in 77-90), and validates the NYSE VW/EW benchmark return computation from CRSP. Also checks the FM intercept magnitudes (large intercepts ~1.7-2.1%/mo).
tables.paper_quote: Table VI shows the average FM slopes for two roughly equal subperiods (July 1963-December 1976 and January 1977-December 1990) from two regressions: (a) the cross-section of stock returns on size, ln(ME), and book-to-market equity, ln(BE/ME), and (b) returns on beta, ln(ME), and ln(BE/ME). For perspective, average returns on the value-weighted and equal-weighted (VW and EW) portfolios of NYSE stocks are also shown.
tables.notes: Complete table targeted (all 81 cells). Prose cross-checks: beta slope 0.10 (t=0.25) 1963-76 and -0.44 (t=-1.17) 1977-90; BE/ME subperiod slopes 0.36 and 0.35 vs 0.35 full period. NYSE VW/EW returns are computed from CRSP NYSE-listed common stocks (shrcd 10/11, exchcd 1) with delisting-adjusted returns — the CRSP msi index includes AMEX/NASDAQ and is not the paper's NYSE-only series.
